content: A study was conducted in which male and female rats were administered oral doses of up to 500 mg/kg/day of a substance, which is approximately 12 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) on a mg/m² basis. At a higher dose of 1250 mg/kg/day (more than 30 times the MRHD on a mg/m² basis), a significant reduction in the number of corpora lutea was observed, leading to a decrease in implantations and live fetuses. Additionally, aspirin was found to inhibit ovulation in rats. The European Stroke Prevention Study 2 (ESPS 2) was a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial conducted over 24 months. It included 6602 patients aged 18 years or older who had experienced an ischemic stroke (76%) or a transient ischemic attack (TIA, 24%) within three months prior to enrollment. Patients were recruited from 13 European countries between February 1989 and May 1995 and were randomized into one of four treatment groups: aspirin and extended-release dipyridamole (25 mg/200 mg), extended-release dipyridamole alone (200 mg), aspirin alone (25 mg), or placebo. Participants took one capsule twice daily, in the morning and evening. The study assessed efficacy by analyzing stroke (fatal or nonfatal) and all-cause mortality, confirmed by a blinded morbidity and mortality assessment group. No significant differences in efficacy were observed based on age or gender, although older patients showed a trend toward more events. The differences in outcomes between the treatment groups were not statistically significant. The incidence rates for aspirin and dipyridamole, as well as aspirin alone, were consistent with previous studies in stroke and TIA patients. Aspirin and dipyridamole capsules are supplied as hard gelatin capsules with a red cap and an ivory-colored body. The capsules contain yellow extended-release pellets of dipyridamole and a round white tablet of immediate-release aspirin. The capsule body is imprinted in red with the Boehringer Ingelheim logo and 01A. They are available in unit-of-use bottles containing 60 capsules (NDC 0597-0001-60). The capsules should be stored at 25°C (77°F), with permissible temperature excursions between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). They must be protected from excessive moisture. Patients should be informed about the general risk of bleeding associated with antiplatelet agents, including intracranial and gastrointestinal bleeding. They should be educated on recognizing signs and symptoms of bleeding, including occult bleeding, and advised to notify their physician if they are prescribed any medications that may increase bleeding risk. Patients who consume three or more alcoholic drinks daily should be counseled about the increased bleeding risks associated with chronic, heavy alcohol use while taking aspirin. Additionally, patients should be informed that aspirin is known to be harmful to fetuses and should notify their physician if they are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Some patients may experience headaches when starting treatment; these are usually transient. If headaches become intolerable, patients should contact their physician. Patients should be instructed to swallow the capsules whole without chewing or crushing them. If a dose is missed, they should continue with the next dose on their regular schedule and avoid taking a double dose. Patients should also be advised to protect the capsules from moisture. The interaction between alcohol and aspirin/dipyridamole has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. The brand name for this combination medication is AGGRENOX®. There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for aspirin and dipyridamole in the drug label.
